hardware: AWS m7g.4xlarge (Graviton3, 16 cores / 64 GB). Gateway-under-test pinned to 4 cores (the comparable basis); mock and load generator on 6 cores each so the mock never bottlenecks the streaming sweep. Ubuntu 24.04. One dedicated box per gateway.

files.helicone.txt:
# ── config.gen.yaml (rendered; loaded via -c config.gen.yaml) ──
server:
  address: 0.0.0.0
  port: 8787
helicone:
  features: none
telemetry:
  exporter: stdout
providers:
  openai:
    base-url: "http://127.0.0.1:8000/"
  anthropic:
    base-url: "http://127.0.0.1:8000/"
  bedrock:
    base-url: "http://127.0.0.1:8000/"
routers:
  default:
    load-balance:
      chat:
        strategy: latency
        providers:
          - openai
          - anthropic
          - bedrock

# ── launch env (non-secret; provider/AWS keys are dummy on the isolated rig) ──
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-dummy
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-dummy
GEMINI_API_KEY=sk-dummy
AWS_ACCESS_KEY=AKIAMOCKACCESSKEY
AWS_SECRET_KEY=mock-secret-access-key
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIAMOCKACCESSKEY
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=mock-secret-access-key
AWS_REGION=us-east-1

matrix.upstream_note: v2: full 6x6. Top-level cells are the openai-egress row for v1 compatibility; the full grid is under upstreams.<egress>.cells keyed by ingress dialect.
matrix.capability_note: advisory context only (probe-first: every cell is probed regardless): Helicone AI Gateway has no OpenAI-Responses converter (endpoints/openai only ChatCompletions), no native Cohere dialect, and its Gemini egress targets Google's OpenAI-compat surface v1beta/openai/chat/completions rather than native generateContent (endpoints/google/generate_contents.rs); those cells are grey by that capability limit

memory.protocol: post-6x6, fresh cold restart: 60s COLD idle (measured before the process serves any request) -> fixed load on the peak cell (c=64, payload=4096B, 120s, identical on every gateway) -> 60s recovery
memory.serve_error: no served cell in the 6x6 sweep
